| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `layers.independent` Sessions and account access are independent: a signed-out request on an API or protocol endpoint carries the Session header, and a signed-in request also carries an access token. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L7) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `layers.verify-before-use` Relying on Session identity, ownership, continuity or state requires verification, and an endpoint that uses no Session claims can handle requests without verifying the header. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L8) | MUST | company |  |

| ! | `layers.operator-not-session` Operator recognition alone does not verify Session claims, authorize account access, or decide whether the Company accepts the request. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L10) | MUST NOT | company |  |

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `discovery.well-known` A Company publishes its `poppy.json` document at `https://{domain}/.well-known/poppy.json` over HTTPS, where `{domain}` is the Company's domain or a subdomain it controls. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L9) | MUST | company | `discovery/poppy-json` |
| – | `discovery.redirect` The well-known URL may redirect, including to another host. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L10) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `discovery.redirect-https` Personal Agents follow redirects, and every redirect is to an HTTPS URL. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L11) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `discovery.final-path` Personal Agents use the document only when the last URL's path is exactly `/.well-known/poppy.json` and it has no query. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L12) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `discovery.https` Every URL the protocol defines or exchanges is an HTTPS URL, in `poppy.json`, authorization-server and protected-resource metadata, client metadata, extensions, assertions, Session JWTs and responses, except the Company's website pages and loopback redirect URIs; Personal Agents do not use a URL from a Company with another scheme, and Companies reject one from a Personal Agent. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L13) | MUST | both | `discovery/poppy-json` |
| → | `discovery.skill-urls` Skill artifact URL references are resolved before the HTTPS rule applies, and the resolved URL is what that rule covers. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L14) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `discovery.redirect-secrets` When the token, revocation or device-authorization endpoint, an API, `{browser_session_endpoint}/authorize`, or a conversation, tasks, feedback or extension endpoint answers with a redirect, the Personal Agent does not send a token, Session JWT, assertion or credentials to the new URL. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L15) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `discovery.private-addresses` Personal Agents and Companies do not connect to a loopback, private or link-local address for a URL the other party gave them, unless configured to on purpose. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L16) | MUST NOT | both | `identity/private-agent-urls` |

## §3.2 OAuth server

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `issuer.sign-in-requires-issuer` A Company that offers sign-in has an OAuth issuer. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L44) | MUST | company |  |
| – | `issuer.signed-out-without-oauth` A Company without an issuer may offer signed-out Sessions, including APIs, conversations, feedback and browser join, without an authorization server. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L45) | MAY | company |  |
| ! | `issuer.identifier` The Company's identifier is its issuer when it has one, and otherwise `https://{organization.domain}` with the host in lowercase and no trailing slash; Session JWTs use it as their audience, and User IDs and Agent IDs are scoped by it. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L46) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `issuer.resource-metadata` A Company with an issuer publishes protected-resource metadata for `https://{organization.domain}` at `https://{organization.domain}/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`, and its `resource` is exactly `https://{organization.domain}`. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L47) | MUST | company |  |
| → | `issuer.no-issuer-signal` HTTP 404, or valid metadata with `authorization_servers` absent or empty, means the Company has no issuer, and that is valid only when `auth.issuer` is absent and the Company offers no sign-in. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L48) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `issuer.no-fallback` A Personal Agent does not use the domain fallback after a timeout, another error status, invalid metadata or a failure to verify an issuer, and does not fall back for a Company whose issuer it already knows unless a successful discovery explicitly establishes that the issuer was removed. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L49) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `issuer.single-server` If protected-resource metadata lists one authorization server, that server is the Company's issuer. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L50) | MUST | both |  |
| ✓ | `issuer.metadata` The issuer publishes OAuth Authorization Server Metadata (RFC 8414) at the URL RFC 8414 defines, and its `protected_resources` lists `https://{domain}` with no path or trailing slash for every domain whose issuer it is. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L51) | MUST | company | `discovery/issuer-metadata` |
| – | `issuer.other-resources` `protected_resources` may list other resources, such as the Company's MCP servers. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L52) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `issuer.agent-check` Before using a Company's `poppy.json`, the Personal Agent checks that the metadata `issuer` matches the issuer it found, character for character, and that `protected_resources` includes `https://{organization.domain}`, compared as RFC 9728 after lowercasing the host. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L53) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `issuer.endpoints` The metadata has `token_endpoint`, `revocation_endpoint` and `grant_types_supported`, plus `authorization_endpoint` when `grant_types_supported` includes `authorization_code` and `device_authorization_endpoint` when it includes the device-code grant. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L54) | MUST | company | `discovery/issuer-metadata` |
| ✓ | `issuer.grant-types` `grant_types_supported` includes `refresh_token`. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L55) | MUST | company | `discovery/issuer-metadata` |
| ! | `issuer.sign-in-grants` `authorization_code` in `grant_types_supported` offers Direct Sign-In, and `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code` offers Device Sign-In. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L56) | MUST | both |  |
| – | `issuer.par` The metadata may list `pushed_authorization_request_endpoint`, and `require_pushed_authorization_requests` set to `true` means Direct Sign-In needs Pushed Authorization Requests. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L57) | MAY | company |  |
| ✓ | `issuer.scopes-supported` A Company that offers sign-in lists every scope a Personal Agent can request in `scopes_supported` of the issuer metadata, of the domain's protected-resource metadata, or of both. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L58) | SHOULD | company | `discovery/issuer-metadata` |
| – | `issuer.resource-scopes` Protected-resource metadata may list `scopes_supported` instead of or as well as the issuer's metadata. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L59) | MAY | company |  |
| – | `issuer.extra-fields` The issuer metadata may have other fields, which Personal Agents ignore. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L60) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `issuer.disabled-sign-in` A Personal Agent does not start Direct, Device or Mediated Sign-In with a Company that sets `auth.disabled`. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L61) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `issuer.disabled-no-mediated` A Company that sets `auth.disabled` does not list the Mediated Sign-In extension or `signed_in` access. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L62) | MUST NOT | company |  |
| ! | `issuer.disabled-reject-refresh` A Company that sets `auth.disabled` and has never issued a refresh token to a Personal Agent answers every refresh with `invalid_grant` and every revocation with success. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L63) | MUST | company |  |
| – | `issuer.disabled-skip-assertion` That Company may answer those refresh and revocation requests without verifying the client assertion, until it has issued a refresh token or turns sign-in on. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L64) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `issuer.identifier-change` If adding or changing an issuer changes the Company's identifier, Personal Agents use new User IDs, Agent IDs and Sessions for the new identifier, and earlier carts and conversations do not transfer automatically. | – | `issuer.shared` Several domains may have the same issuer, and they are then one Company sharing User IDs, Sessions and refresh tokens. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L66) | MAY | company |  |
| ! | `issuer.same-issuer` The Company selects that same issuer on each of those domains. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L67) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `issuer.same-scope-meaning` The Company gives each scope the same authorization meaning across domains that share an issuer. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L68) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `issuer.same-scope-text` The Company publishes the same scope descriptions and hints across those domains. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L69) | SHOULD | company |  |
| – | `issuer.different-capabilities` Those domains may expose different scopes or capabilities, and other fields may differ by domain. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L70) | MAY | company |  |
| ✎ | `issuer.one-company` An issuer represents exactly one Company, and a provider that hosts several Companies gives each its own issuer, even on shared servers. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L71) | MUST | company | _each definePoppyseed is one Company, whose issuer is its own baseUrl; a provider runs one per Company_ |
| – | `discovery.access-hint` A `poppy` entry may set `access` to `session`, the default, or `signed_in`. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L72) | MAY | company |  |
| ! | `discovery.signed-in-hint` A Company that lists `signed_in` has an issuer and does not set `auth.disabled`. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L73) | MUST | company |  |
| → | `discovery.unknown-access` Personal Agents ignore unknown `access` values and handle them as an absent hint. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L74) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `discovery.access-not-permission` An `access` hint grants no permission; runtime challenges and authorization events remain authoritative. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L75) | MUST | both |  |

## §3.3 Extensions

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `extensions.naming` Extensions defined with this protocol have plain names, such as `operations`; anyone else starts an extension's name with a domain they control, such as `example.com/gift-wrap`. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L79) | MUST | both | `discovery/extension-names` |
| ✓ | `extensions.version` Each extension entry has a `version`, the extension's major version; incompatible changes get a new version, and changes implementations can safely ignore keep the version. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L80) | MUST | both | `discovery/extension-names` |
| → | `extensions.declare` A Personal Agent declares the extensions it uses with a Company, one version of each, in the `Poppy-Extensions` header, and does not need to declare an extension the Company recognizes from the request itself. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L81) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `extensions.ignore-unknown` Personal Agents and Companies ignore extensions and versions they do not support and fields they do not recognize. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L82) | MUST | both | `extensions/ignore-unknown` |
| ! | `extensions.schema` An extension that defines conversation-message content publishes a JSON Schema for that content. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L83) | MUST | both |  |
| – | `extensions.required` A Company may refuse a request it handles only with an extension the request does not declare, in a version the Company lists, unless the request itself uses the extension, returning `extension_required` (HTTP 403) with the extension's name in `extension`. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L84) | MAY | company |  |
| ✓ | `extensions.required-shape` `extension_required` is a JSON body, both at APIs and at endpoints this protocol or an extension defines, and it is not an access-token error, so it does not go in `WWW-Authenticate`. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L85) | MUST | company | `ops/require-extension` |

## §3.4 Versions

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `versions.same-host` Each URL in `supported_versions` is an HTTPS URL on the host that served `poppy.json`, after any redirects. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L89) | MUST | company |  |
| → | `versions.no-foreign-document` A Personal Agent does not use a `supported_versions` document whose URL is on another host, and does not follow a redirect from it. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L90) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `versions.listed-version` A Personal Agent does not use a linked document whose `protocol_version` is not the version it is listed under, and that document has no `supported_versions` of its own. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L91) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `versions.same-company` Every document a Company serves at the same time has the same `organization.domain` and selects the same issuer. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L92) | MUST | company |  |
| – | `versions.other-fields` Other fields may differ by version. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L93) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `versions.choose` The Personal Agent chooses the newest version, among `protocol_version` and `supported_versions`, that is compatible with one it implements, and does not use any of them if none is; two versions are compatible when they have the same major version and, before 1.0, the same minor version. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L94) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `versions.header` On every request with the Session header, the Personal Agent sends `Poppy-Version` as `major.minor`, a version it implements that is compatible with the chosen one. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L95) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `versions.extensions-header` When it uses extensions, it also sends `Poppy-Extensions` as an RFC 9651 List of Strings, each an extension name from the chosen document with the version it uses in the `v` parameter. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L96) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `versions.no-extensions-header` Without `Poppy-Extensions`, or when it fails to parse, the request declares no extensions. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L97) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `versions.stable-session` The Personal Agent sends the same `Poppy-Version` and `Poppy-Extensions` on every request in a Session, and starts a new Session to change them. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L98) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `versions.check` An endpoint that verifies the Session header also checks `Poppy-Version`, and rejects a missing header or a version that is not compatible with one the Company serves with `version_unsupported` (HTTP 400, JSON body). [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L99) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `versions.no-other-version` That endpoint does not handle the rejected request under another version. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L100) | MUST NOT | company |  |
| → | `versions.retry` After `version_unsupported`, the Personal Agent fetches `poppy.json` again without using a cached copy and chooses again; if it chooses another version, it starts a new Session and sends the request again, once, and otherwise it stops sending the request. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L101) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| – | `versions.sunset` A Company that plans to stop serving a version may say so with the `Deprecation` and `Sunset` headers. [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L102) | MAY | company |  |
| ! | `versions.stable-meaning` From 1.0, the location of `poppy.json` and how it is fetched, `protocol_version`, `supported_versions`, `Poppy-Version` and `version_unsupported` keep their meaning in every version. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/03-discovery.md#L103) | MUST | both |  |

## §4 OAuth

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `oauth.prefer-direct` A Company that offers sign-in offers Direct Sign-In. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L9) | SHOULD | company |  |
| → | `oauth.agent-prefer-direct` A Personal Agent uses Direct Sign-In when the Company offers it. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L10) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| – | `oauth.refuse-client` A Company may turn off sign-in for every Personal Agent, or refuse sign-in or one sign-in type by `client_id`. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L11) | MAY | company |  |

## §4 Browser control marking steps

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `bctl.mark-values` `data-poppy-user-step` of `interaction` leaves changing or activating a control, or a form's controls and submitting it, to the User; `submission` on a form lets the browser fill controls unless other marks say not to, and leaves submitting to the User; any other value, or `submission` on anything but a form, counts as `interaction`. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/ext-browser-control.md#L17) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `bctl.mark-all` The Company marks every control that performs the step, or the form it is in, and marks them before they can be used. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-browser-control.md#L18) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `bctl.submission-not-perform` The Company does not let filling in a `submission` form perform the step itself. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-browser-control.md#L19) | SHOULD NOT | company |  |
| ! | `bctl.server-checks` The Company's servers check the action's conditions themselves, because marks do not stop anything. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-browser-control.md#L20) | MUST | company |  |

## §4 Mediated Sign-In one-time codes

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `mediated.code-step` When the Company returns `code_required` with `sign_in_id`, the Personal Agent sends the same grant again with `sign_in_id` and `one_time_code` and its client assertion, and not the credentials or `scope`; a wrong code returns `code_required` again until the attempt limit, then `invalid_grant`. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/ext-mediated-sign-in.md#L23) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `mediated.same-client` Only the `client_id` that started a sign-in can finish it. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/ext-mediated-sign-in.md#L24) | MUST | company |  |

## §4 UCP identity and authorization

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `ucp.same-profile-url` Where a transport carries the platform profile in more than one place, the Personal Agent sends the same URL in each. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-ucp.md#L22) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `ucp.reject-profile-mismatch` The Company rejects a request where those profile URLs differ. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-ucp.md#L23) | MUST | company |  |
| → | `ucp.operator-signature` The Personal Agent signs UCP requests with an HTTP Message Signature, as it should for every request that carries the Session header. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-ucp.md#L24) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| – | `ucp.verify-session` A Company may verify the Session header on UCP requests. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-ucp.md#L25) | MAY | company |  |
| ! | `ucp.verify-before-claims` The Company verifies the header before relying on any Session claim. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-ucp.md#L26) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ucp.bearer` When a UCP request is signed in, the access token is a Bearer token, and the Company returns `token_type` `Bearer` for tokens for its UCP services. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/ext-ucp.md#L27) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ucp.one-sign-in` A Company that offers both this protocol's sign-in and UCP identity linking offers Direct Sign-In, and lists `private_key_jwt` in `token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported`. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-ucp.md#L28) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ucp.scopes-listed` The Company lists each scope in its identity-linking `config.scopes` in `scopes_supported`. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-ucp.md#L29) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ucp.describe-scopes` The Company describes each such scope and gives `auth.scope_hints` for it. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-ucp.md#L30) | SHOULD | company |  |
| → | `ucp.no-foreign-token` A Personal Agent does not send a token it got independently of this extension on a request that carries the Session header. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-ucp.md#L31) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `ucp.insufficient-scope` For UCP `insufficient_scope`, the Personal Agent requests every scope it still needs, including scopes it already has and wants to keep, and the Company grants only the scopes the request names. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/ext-ucp.md#L32) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §4.1 Agent identity

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `identity.client-id-url` A Personal Agent's `client_id` is an HTTPS URL that returns its client metadata document. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L15) | MUST | both | `identity/client-id-is-url` |
| ✓ | `identity.client-id-matches` `client_id` in the metadata equals the URL the document was fetched from. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L16) | MUST | both | `identity/client-id-must-match` |
| ! | `identity.jwks` `jwks_uri` is an HTTPS URL on the same domain as `client_id`, and the key set contains only public keys. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L17) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `identity.redirect-uris` Each `redirect_uris` entry is an HTTPS URL on the same domain as `client_id`, or a loopback redirect URI as RFC 8252 §7.3 defines. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L18) | MUST | both |  |
| ✓ | `identity.loopback-redirect` Companies accept loopback redirect URIs in `redirect_uris`. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L19) | MUST | company | `identity/loopback-redirect` |
| ✓ | `identity.private-key-jwt` The Personal Agent authenticates at the token endpoint with a client assertion signed by a key from `jwks_uri` (`private_key_jwt`, RFC 7523); Session JWTs are signed with delegated keys instead. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L20) | MUST | both | `identity/client-auth-required`<br>`identity/client-assertion-claims`<br>`identity/client-assertion-replay` |
| ✓ | `identity.client-assertion-aud` The client assertion's `aud` is the Company's issuer as a single string, and Companies reject any other `aud`, compared character for character, including their token endpoint URL. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L21) | MUST | both | `identity/client-assertion-claims` |
| → | `identity.client-assertion-fresh` A client assertion is short-lived and includes `iat` and a unique, unguessable `jti`. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L22) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `identity.client-assertion-replay` The Company may reject a reused client-assertion `jti`. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L23) | MAY | company | `identity/client-assertion-replay` |
| ! | `identity.algorithms` Companies accept client assertions signed with `ES256` and with `PS384`. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L24) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `identity.refused` A refused Personal Agent gets `invalid_client` at the authorization server, or `invalid_session` at a resource. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L25) | MUST | company |  |
| – | `identity.unauthorized-client` A Company may accept a Personal Agent for signed-out Sessions but refuse it sign-in, or one sign-in type, with `unauthorized_client`. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L26) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `identity.choose-companies` A Personal Agent decides which Companies it uses the protocol with, and the requirements on Personal Agents apply when it does. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L27) | MAY | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §4.2 Direct Sign-In

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `direct.redirect-exact` `redirect_uri` exactly matches an entry in the Personal Agent's `redirect_uris`, except for the port of a loopback redirect URI. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L33) | MUST | company | `identity/loopback-redirect`<br>`direct/redirect-exact` |
| ✓ | `direct.redirect-iss` The redirect back carries the Company's issuer in `iss`, including on `error=access_denied`. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L34) | MUST | company | `direct/sign-in`<br>`direct/decline` |
| → | `direct.check-iss` The Personal Agent checks that `iss` exactly matches the issuer of the Company it started sign-in with. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L35) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `direct.client-assertion` The token request carries the Personal Agent's client assertion. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L36) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `direct.prompt-consent` Unless the Personal Agent receives the redirect only on the device that opened the authorization URL, the authorization request includes `prompt=consent`. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L37) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `direct.support-prompt` The Company supports `prompt=consent`, whether or not it supports OpenID Connect, and shows its consent page for a request that includes it, even when the account already granted every requested scope to the `client_id`. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L38) | SHOULD | company |  |
| – | `direct.ignore-unknown-prompt` A Company that does not support `prompt=consent` ignores it. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L39) | MAY | company |  |
| – | `direct.require-par` A Company may require Pushed Authorization Requests by setting `require_pushed_authorization_requests` to `true`. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L40) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `direct.use-par` When the Company requires PAR, the Personal Agent sends the authorization parameters to `pushed_authorization_request_endpoint` with its client assertion, and opens `authorization_endpoint` with only `client_id` and `request_uri`. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L41) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `direct.prefer-par` A Personal Agent uses PAR whenever the metadata lists `pushed_authorization_request_endpoint`. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L42) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `direct.par-dpop` A Personal Agent that sends DPoP proofs sends one with the pushed request, so the Company can bind the code to the key. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L43) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `direct.par-link` When the Personal Agent sends the User a link to open later, the link goes to a page of its own that pushes the request when the User opens it and then redirects to `authorization_endpoint`. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L44) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `direct.cross-device` Companies that offer Direct Sign-In, and Personal Agents that open the authorization URL on a device other than the one the User is using, follow the best practices in RFC 10027 §2. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L45) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `direct.same-device` A Personal Agent receives the redirect only on the device that opened the authorization URL when it can. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L46) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §4.3 Device Sign-In

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `device.cross-device` Companies that offer Device Sign-In and Personal Agents that use it follow the best practices in RFC 10027 §2, including its guidance on when to use the device authorization grant. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L50) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `device.show-link` Before showing `verification_uri` and `user_code`, or `verification_uri_complete`, the Personal Agent checks that the link's host is the host of the Company's issuer or `organization.domain`, or a subdomain of either, and shows the Company's `organization.name` and domain with them. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L51) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `device.keep-code-private` The Personal Agent keeps `device_code` private. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L52) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `device.open-not-approve` Opening the verification link does not approve the request by itself. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L53) | MUST NOT | company | `device/sign-in` |
| ✓ | `device.consent` The Company shows its consent page for every Device Sign-In request, even when the account already granted every requested scope to the `client_id`. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L54) | SHOULD | company | `device/sign-in` |
| → | `device.client-assertion` Each poll carries the client assertion. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L55) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §4.4 Refresh tokens

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `refresh.downscope` A refresh request may send `scope` to ask for fewer scopes than the refresh token has, and `resource` for a token for one service. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L59) | MAY | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `refresh.rotation` The Personal Agent uses a new refresh token if the response has one, and keeps the old one otherwise. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L60) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `refresh.not-a-session` A refresh token is not tied to a Session, and any of the User's Sessions can use access tokens from it. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L61) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `refresh.same-dpop-key` A Personal Agent that sends a DPoP proof when it gets a refresh token sends a proof from the same key with every refresh of that refresh token and of the refresh tokens that replace it, and keeps the key unless the User signs in again or an extension the Company requires defines how to replace it. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L62) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| – | `refresh.bind-dpop` A Company may bind a refresh token to the key of the DPoP proof in the request that issued it, and the refresh tokens that replace it, and then rejects a refresh whose proof is missing or from another key with `invalid_grant` and issues nothing bound to that key, except through such an extension's replacement procedure. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L63) | MAY | company |  |

## §4.5 Access tokens

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `tokens.authorization-scheme` A signed-in request carries an access token in the `Authorization` header with the scheme the token response's `token_type` names. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L67) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `tokens.support-dpop` Personal Agents support DPoP. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L68) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `tokens.send-dpop` A Personal Agent that supports DPoP sends a DPoP proof with its token requests when the issuer's metadata lists `dpop_signing_alg_values_supported`. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L69) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `tokens.dpop-one-user` The Personal Agent uses each DPoP key for one User ID only, and keeps it for every refresh of the refresh tokens it got with it. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L70) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| – | `tokens.bearer-choice` The Company decides for each token whether to bind it, and returns `token_type` `Bearer` for one it does not bind. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L71) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `tokens.session-ath` A signed-in request also carries the Session header, whose `ath` covers the access token. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L72) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `tokens.resource-metadata` Before its first signed-in call to an API or a conversation endpoint, the Personal Agent fetches that service's protected-resource metadata and uses it only if `resource` is the URL it derived the metadata URL from. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L73) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `tokens.resource-parameter` If that metadata exists and its `resource` is not `https://{organization.domain}`, the Personal Agent requests a token with `resource` set to it and uses that token only there. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L74) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `tokens.resource-only-there` The Company accepts a token issued for a `resource` only at that service, and returns `invalid_target` for a `resource` it does not serve. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L75) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `tokens.wrong-resource` A service that gets a token not issued for it returns `invalid_token` with `resource_metadata` in its challenge. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L76) | MUST | company |  |

## §4.6 Revocation

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `revoke.refresh` The Personal Agent revokes a refresh token at `revocation_endpoint` with `token_type_hint=refresh_token` and its client assertion. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L80) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `revoke.sign-out` Revoking every refresh token it holds for an account signs out. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L81) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §4.7 Scopes and token responses

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `scopes.browser-sign-in` The protocol defines one scope, `poppy:browser-sign-in`, which lets the Personal Agent sign its browser in to the Company's website; each Company defines its other scopes. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L85) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `scopes.extra-sources` The Personal Agent may also request scopes documented by the Company's APIs or sign-in extensions, even when absent from both `scopes_supported` lists. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L86) | MAY | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| – | `scopes.hidden` Either `scopes_supported` list may leave out scopes the Company offers only to its other clients, and the Company may limit the scopes it grants by client. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L87) | MAY | company |  |
| ! | `scopes.describe` The Company describes each scope it offers Personal Agents, in an OpenAPI OAuth security scheme it lists or otherwise in `auth.scopes`, and when both describe a scope the Personal Agent uses `auth.scopes`. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L88) | SHOULD | company |  |
| – | `scopes.hints` A Company may give hints about any scope in `auth.scope_hints`, with `changes` of `none`, `reversible` or `irreversible` and `personal_data` true or false, describing the most consequential action that requires the scope. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L89) | MAY | company |  |
| ! | `scopes.hint-fields` A Company includes both `changes` and `personal_data` in each `auth.scope_hints` entry. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L90) | MUST | company |  |
| → | `scopes.unknown-hints` A Personal Agent ignores hint fields it does not recognize, and treats a `changes` value it does not recognize as `irreversible`. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L91) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `scopes.no-extra` The Company does not grant scopes beyond those requested. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L92) | MUST NOT | company |  |
| → | `scopes.request-scope` Each sign-in request includes `scope`, except where an extension continues an earlier request, as a space-separated string. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L93) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `scopes.invalid-scope` Missing or unknown scopes are rejected with `invalid_scope`. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L94) | MUST | company |  |
| – | `scopes.fewer` The Company may grant fewer scopes than requested, and the response's `scope` says which it granted. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L95) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `scopes.least` A Personal Agent requests only the scopes the User's tasks need. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L96) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `scopes.reauthorize-all` If a task needs more access than the refresh token allows, the Personal Agent requests every scope it still needs, including previously granted scopes it wants to keep, and does not request only the missing scopes. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L97) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `scopes.revoke-replaced` The Personal Agent revokes the refresh token that the new one replaces, and revoking a replaced refresh token is not sign-out. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L98) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `scopes.pending-unchanged` A pending or failed sign-in leaves existing tokens unchanged. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L99) | MUST | both |  |
| – | `scopes.refresh-rotation` Refresh may return a replacement refresh token. [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L100) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `scopes.check-response` The Personal Agent checks `scope` before continuing; the response leaves `scope` out only when the Company granted exactly the scopes requested. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L101) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `scopes.at-least-one` A Poppy sign-in grants at least one scope; if the User approves none, it ends as a decline. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/04-oauth.md#L102) | MUST | company |  |

## §5 Sessions

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `sessions.first-request` There is no separate step to start a Session: the first request with a new `sid` starts it. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L14) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `sessions.signed-in-per-request` A Session is signed out unless the request carries an access token. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L15) | MUST | both |  |

## §5 Browser control handing control to the User

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `bctl.no-take-step` A Personal Agent that declares this extension does not take a marked step, and does not remove or change marks to get around them. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-browser-control.md#L24) | SHOULD NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `bctl.leave-undone` When it reaches a marked step, the Personal Agent may leave the step undone and continue with other work. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-browser-control.md#L25) | MAY | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `bctl.model-while-user` While the User holds control, the Personal Agent's software does not carry out browser actions from its model. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-browser-control.md#L26) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `bctl.only-user-ends` Only the User ends their control; a timeout, a change to the page's marks, or anything the Company sends does not end it. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-browser-control.md#L27) | MUST NOT | both |  |
| → | `bctl.no-wait` The Personal Agent does not keep its own requests, or its conversation with the User, waiting until the User acts. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-browser-control.md#L28) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §5 UCP conversations through Ask

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `ucp.ask-listed` A Company that lists a `ucp` conversation entry lists this extension, and its UCP profile offers `dev.ucp.common.ask`. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-ucp.md#L36) | MUST | company |  |
| – | `ucp.ask-conversation` A Company may return a `conversation` so follow-up questions build on earlier turns. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-ucp.md#L37) | MAY | company |  |
| – | `ucp.also-poppy` A Company may list a `poppy` conversation entry too. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-ucp.md#L38) | MAY | company |  |

## §5.1 User IDs and Agent IDs

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `sessions.user-id-stable` The Personal Agent gives each of its Users a User ID for each Company, using the Company's identifier; the ID is stable, opaque and different for each Company. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L19) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `sessions.user-id-no-pii` A User ID does not contain or derive from personal information, such as an email address, phone number or name, even with a keyed hash. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L20) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `sessions.anonymous` A Personal Agent may give a User a new User ID for each anonymous browsing session, uses that ID for nothing else, and discards it when the browsing session ends. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L21) | MAY | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `sessions.anonymous-no-sign-in` A Personal Agent does not send an access token in a Session that uses an anonymous browsing User ID. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L22) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `sessions.agent-id` A Personal Agent that acts for a User through several agents it runs may name which one a Session is for with an Agent ID, and one with a single agent leaves it out. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L23) | MAY | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `sessions.agent-id-no-pii` An Agent ID is stable, opaque and different for each Company, and does not contain or derive from personal information. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L24) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| – | `sessions.agent-id-use` The Company may use the Agent ID to tell a User's agents apart, while they share the User's account, refresh tokens and conversations. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L25) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `sessions.user-id-confidential` The Personal Agent keeps the mapping of each User's User IDs and Agent IDs across Companies confidential: it does not publish it or share it with third parties, other than service providers that process it on its behalf. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L26) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §5.2 The Session header

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `session.header-required` The Personal Agent sends a `Poppy-Session` header on every request to a Company's APIs, conversations and other resource endpoints this protocol or an extension defines, using destinations from `poppy.json`. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L30) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `session.header-elsewhere` The Personal Agent does not send a Company's Session JWT to any other destination, except the website pages this section allows, and discovery, description documents and OAuth endpoints do not carry the header. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L31) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `session.version-with-header` Requests that carry the Session header also carry `Poppy-Version`, and `Poppy-Extensions` when the Personal Agent uses extensions with the Company. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L32) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `session.typ` The Session JWT's `typ` is `poppy-session+jwt`. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L33) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `session.alg` The Session JWT's `alg` is `ES256`, it is signed with a delegated key, `kid` is that key's JWK thumbprint, and `poppy_dlg` carries its delegation. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L34) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `session.claims` `iss` is the Personal Agent's `client_id`, `aud` is the Company's identifier as a single string, `sub` is the User ID, `htm` and `htu` are the request's method and URL without the query or fragment, `iat` is when it was signed, and `jti` is unique and unguessable. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L35) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `session.sid` The Personal Agent chooses `sid` at random so it cannot be guessed, and does not use it for any other Session. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L36) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `session.ath` `ath` is the base64url SHA-256 hash of the access token when the request carries one, and is left out otherwise. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L37) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `session.required-claims` The Personal Agent includes every claim except `agent_id`, and except `ath` when there is no access token. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L38) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `session.same-subject` The Personal Agent sends the same `sub` and `agent_id`, or no `agent_id`, in every Session JWT for a Session. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L39) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `session.page-fetch` A Personal Agent that fetches a page of the Company's website with its own HTTP client, rather than a browser, sends the Session header, only for HTTPS URLs whose host is exactly `organization.domain`. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L40) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `session.page-no-token` The Personal Agent does not send an access token with those page fetches, so the request is signed out. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L41) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `session.page-redirect` When a page redirects, the Personal Agent signs a new Session JWT for the new URL only if its host is still `organization.domain`, and otherwise follows the redirect without the header. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L42) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `session.page-retry-without` After a page that verifies the header rejects a failed check with `invalid_session`, the Personal Agent may fetch the page again without the header. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L43) | MAY | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `delegation.algorithms` Companies accept delegations signed with `ES256` and with `PS384`. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L44) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `delegation.typ` A delegation's `typ` is `poppy-delegation+jwt`. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L45) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `delegation.no-private` `cnf.jwk` does not contain private key members. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L46) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `delegation.lifetime` A delegation's `exp` is at most 24 hours after `iat`. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L47) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `delegation.no-user` A Personal Agent does not put a User ID, an Agent ID, a Company's issuer, or anything else about the User or the Companies they use in a delegation. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L48) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `delegation.no-late-sign` The Personal Agent does not sign a Session JWT after its delegation's `exp`. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L49) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `delegation.reject` When verifying a Session header, the Company rejects, with `invalid_session`, a Session JWT without a delegation, including one signed directly with a key from `jwks_uri`, and a Session JWT whose delegation fails the delegation checks. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L50) | MUST | company |  |
| – | `delegation.cache` A resource may cache a verified delegation until it expires. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L51) | MAY | company |  |
| ! | `delegation.key-not-stable` A Company does not expect a User's delegated key to stay the same between requests or Sessions, and does not treat a new one as a reason to reject a request. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L52) | MUST NOT | company |  |
| → | `delegation.one-user` The Personal Agent uses each delegated key, and its delegation, for one User ID only. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L53) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| – | `delegation.reject-second-user` A Company may reject, with `invalid_session`, a Session JWT whose delegated key has already signed for a different User ID while a delegation for the key lasts. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L54) | MAY | company |  |

## §5.3 Verifying the Session header

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `session.verify` Companies verify the Session header on every request that carries it. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L58) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `session.verify-before-use` The Company completes the Session checks before relying on Session claims for client or User identity, ownership, continuity, or access to state, including creating or continuing a Session. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L59) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `session.fetch-client` Verification fetches the client metadata from `iss` without following redirects and the public keys from its `jwks_uri`, following the address checks in section 3. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L60) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `session.check-claims` Verification checks `typ`, that `aud` is the Company's identifier compared character for character, that `htm` and `htu` match the request, and that `iat` is within an acceptance window the Company chooses; the JWT never grants account access. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L61) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `session.check-ath` If the request carries an access token, the Company checks that `ath` matches it and that the token was issued to the same `client_id` as `iss`; without an access token, `ath` is absent. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L62) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `session.lookup` The Company looks up the Session by `client_id`, `sid` and User ID; an unknown combination starts a signed-out Session, and a known one continues it, including the ended-Session check. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L63) | MUST | company |  |
| – | `session.skip-unused` An endpoint that uses no Session claims may handle a request without verifying the header or requiring one. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L64) | MAY | company |  |
| ! | `session.no-unverified-use` The Company does not use unverified Session claims to attribute a request to a Personal Agent, User or Session, or to look up their state. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L65) | MUST NOT | company |  |
| ! | `session.errors` A failed Session check returns HTTP 400 with `{"error": "invalid_session"}`, and an ended Session returns `{"error": "session_ended"}`; either may include `error_description`. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L66) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `session.missing` The Company rejects a request without the Session header when handling it depends on Session claims. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L67) | MUST | company |  |
| – | `session.replay` A Company may reject a reused Session JWT `jti`. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L68) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `session.operator-signature` A Personal Agent also signs requests that carry the Session header with an HTTP Message Signature using Web Bot Auth. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L69) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `session.operator-covers` The operator signature covers `poppy-session`, and `authorization` when present. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L70) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `session.operator-not-session` An operator signature's absence does not make a Session JWT invalid, and verifying it does not replace verifying the Session JWT. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L71) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `session.operator-independent` Before trusting any Session claim, the Company verifies the Session JWT independently. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L72) | MUST | company |  |

## §5.4 Signing in

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `signin.anonymous-token` The Personal Agent does not send an access token in a Session that uses an anonymous browsing User ID. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L76) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| – | `signin.reject-account-change` A Company may reject a request whose access token is for a different account than its Session used before, with `session_ended`. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L77) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `signin.new-session-for-account` A Personal Agent starts a new Session rather than use a second account in one Session. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L78) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `signin.user-present` A Personal Agent uses Direct or Device Sign-In only when the User signs in themselves. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L79) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| – | `signin.revoke-misuse` A Company may revoke a `client_id` that does not follow that rule. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L80) | MAY | company |  |
| ! | `signin.challenge` A request without an access token is signed out, so an account action without one gets a challenge, and an access token without the needed scopes gets `insufficient_scope`. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L81) | MUST | company |  |

## §5.5 Ending Sessions and signing out

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `sessions.lifetime` The Company decides how long a Session lasts and keeps its record only that long. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L85) | MUST | company |  |
| ✓ | `sessions.remember-ended` A Company may remember the `sid`s of Sessions it ended, and a request for a remembered ended Session gets `session_ended` (HTTP 400). [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L86) | MAY | company | `sessions/ended-session` |
| → | `sessions.session-ended-retry` After `session_ended`, the Personal Agent starts a new Session with a new `sid` and sends the request again in it; if the new Session gets `session_ended` too, it stops sending the request. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L87) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `signout.revoke-all` The Personal Agent signs out of an account by revoking every refresh token it holds for it. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L88) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `signout.sessions-continue` The Sessions that used those refresh tokens continue signed out: the Personal Agent sends the Session header without an access token. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L89) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `signout.learn` The Personal Agent finds out the User disconnected it when a request fails with `invalid_token` or refresh returns `invalid_grant`, and then continues signed out. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L90) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `signout.after` After sign-out, what does not need the account carries on; anything that used the account stays as it is, but a request on it without an access token for that account gets a challenge, and a conversation stays open. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L91) | MUST | company | `ops/access`<br>`conv/account-bound` |
| → | `signout.no-resignin` The Personal Agent does not sign in to that account again unless the User asks. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L92) | SHOULD NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §5.6 Sending requests

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `requests.no-cookie` Companies accept the Session header and access token at their APIs, conversations and other protocol and extension endpoints without requiring cookies. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L96) | MUST | company |  |
| → | `requests.no-impersonate` Personal Agents do not leave out the Session header to appear as a person, including on website pages they fetch without a browser, other than fetching a page again after `invalid_session`. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L97) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `requests.not-in-url` Personal Agents do not send tokens or Session JWTs in a URL, and Companies do not accept them from one. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L98) | MUST NOT | both |  |
| ! | `requests.rate-limit` A Company that limits request rate returns HTTP 429 with a `Retry-After` header when a request goes over the limit. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L99) | MUST | company |  |
| → | `requests.retry-after` The Personal Agent waits at least as long as `Retry-After` says before sending that request again. [↗](pap-1.0/05-sessions.md#L100) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §6 Web browsing

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `web.join-before-browse` When the Company lists `web.browser_session_endpoint`, the Personal Agent joins its browser to a Session before browsing the Company's website; without the endpoint, it browses as an ordinary signed-out visitor. [↗](pap-1.0/06-web.md#L7) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `web.disabled` A Personal Agent does not use a browser on the website of a Company that sets `web.disabled`. [↗](pap-1.0/06-web.md#L8) | SHOULD NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `web.disabled-shape` A Company that sets `web.disabled` does not list `browser_session_endpoint`, and lists `agent` or `apis`. [↗](pap-1.0/06-web.md#L9) | MUST NOT | company |  |
| → | `web.own-browser` The Personal Agent joins only a browser it controls to a Session, never the User's own browser. [↗](pap-1.0/06-web.md#L10) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `web.code` The Company makes the browser-join code unguessable and short-lived, and each code works once. [↗](pap-1.0/06-web.md#L11) | MUST | company | `web/page` |
| ✓ | `web.join-cookie` The Company ties the code to the browser that loaded the page with a cookie set in the same response; the cookie is not sent with a form submitted from another site, and other hosts on the Company's domain cannot set it. [↗](pap-1.0/06-web.md#L12) | MUST | company | `web/page` |
| ! | `web.page-isolation` The browser-join page is not stored by caches, framed by other pages, or kept as a window reference by the page that opened it. [↗](pap-1.0/06-web.md#L13) | MUST NOT | company |  |
| ! | `web.page-no-session` Loading the browser-join page does not start, end or change any Session, or change the browser's other cookies. [↗](pap-1.0/06-web.md#L14) | MUST NOT | company |  |
| ! | `web.authorize-checks` The authorize request checks the Session header and the access token if any, checks that the code was issued, has not expired and has not been authorized before, and then records it for that Session. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/06-web.md#L15) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `web.authorize-error` A code that fails those checks gets HTTP 400 with `{"error": "invalid_request"}`. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/06-web.md#L16) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `web.browser-scope` The Company rejects an access token in the authorize step that does not have `poppy:browser-sign-in`, with `insufficient_scope`. [↗](pap-1.0/06-web.md#L17) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `web.support-browser-scope` A Company that lists `browser_session_endpoint` and offers sign-in supports `poppy:browser-sign-in`, though it may grant it to fewer clients or Users. [↗](pap-1.0/06-web.md#L18) | MUST | company |  |
| → | `web.request-browser-scope` A Personal Agent requests `poppy:browser-sign-in` only from a Company that lists `browser_session_endpoint`. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/06-web.md#L19) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `web.code-from-page` The Personal Agent takes the code only from the page its own browser loaded from the endpoint, and does not authorize a code from anywhere else. [↗](pap-1.0/06-web.md#L20) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `web.code-outside-model` The Personal Agent reads the code and sends the authorize request in software its model cannot read. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/06-web.md#L21) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `web.submit-checks` On form submit, the Company checks that the request has the cookie from the page load and that it matches `code`, and that the code was authorized, has not expired and has not been submitted before; a code is used by the first request that submits it. [↗](pap-1.0/06-web.md#L22) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `web.submit-result` If every submit check passes, the Company sets its cookie for that Session, clears the join cookie and redirects the browser to a page on its website; otherwise it sets no cookie and returns an error page with an error status. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/06-web.md#L23) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `web.keep-login` In a join without an access token, the Company does not end or change a login the browser already has. [↗](pap-1.0/06-web.md#L24) | SHOULD NOT | company |  |
| ! | `web.replace-login` A join with an access token signs the browser in to the account from the authorize step, with its scopes, in place of any login it had. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/06-web.md#L25) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `web.cookie-only-step-3` The Session's cookie is set only in the form-submit step. [↗](pap-1.0/06-web.md#L26) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `web.cookie-account` The cookie acts for the account and scopes authorized in the authorize step, if any, and stops acting for the account when the User signs out or disconnects the Personal Agent. [↗](pap-1.0/06-web.md#L27) | MUST | company |  |
| ✓ | `web.cookie-lifetime` The Session's cookie does not outlive the Session. [↗](pap-1.0/06-web.md#L28) | MUST NOT | company | `web/follows-session` |
| ! | `web.apply-scopes` After a signed-in join, the website either applies the cookie's scopes, or treats `poppy:browser-sign-in` as access to everything the account can do on the website. [↗](pap-1.0/06-web.md#L29) | MUST | company |  |
| – | `web.grant-without-ask` When the website applies the cookie's scopes, the Company may grant `poppy:browser-sign-in` without asking the User. [↗](pap-1.0/06-web.md#L30) | MAY | company |  |
| ! | `web.describe-unscoped` When `poppy:browser-sign-in` gives the account's full access on the website, the Company describes it that way, and in Direct and Device Sign-In asks the User to approve it like any other scope. [↗](pap-1.0/06-web.md#L31) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `web.unscoped-flag` A Company whose website treats `poppy:browser-sign-in` as the account's full access sets `web.unscoped` to `true`, and lists `browser_session_endpoint`. [↗](pap-1.0/06-web.md#L32) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `web.unscoped-domains` If any website of domains that share an issuer is unscoped, each of them sets `web.unscoped`. [↗](pap-1.0/06-web.md#L33) | MUST | company |  |
| ✎ | `web.missing-scope` When the website refuses an action because the Session lacks a scope, it shows a visible error message that names the missing scopes. [↗](pap-1.0/06-web.md#L34) | SHOULD | company | _the Company's own pages; browserSession() gives them the Session's scopes, and the reference company's /account names the scope it needs_ |
| → | `web.rejoin` The Personal Agent may join again at any time, and each join replaces the cookie the Company set before. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/06-web.md#L35) | MAY | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §6 Browser control who controls the browser

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `bctl.controller` On pages of the Company's website, in a browser joined to a Session that declared this version, the Personal Agent's software provides `navigator.poppy.controller` as `"user"` while the User holds control and `"agent"` otherwise, set by software rather than the model, and only on the hosts of `organization.domain` and its subdomains. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/ext-browser-control.md#L32) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| – | `bctl.send-controller` The page may send `navigator.poppy.controller` to the Company with the request. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-browser-control.md#L33) | MAY | company |  |
| ! | `bctl.not-a-guarantee` The Company does not rely on `"user"` as a guarantee that the User took the step. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-browser-control.md#L34) | MUST NOT | company |  |

## §6 Mediated Sign-In security

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `mediated.credentials-destination` Personal Agents do not send credentials anywhere other than the `token_endpoint` of the Company's issuer, with this grant. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-mediated-sign-in.md#L28) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `mediated.choose-by-issuer` A Personal Agent chooses which stored credentials to send by the Company's issuer, never by the field labels or the endpoint, and shows the Company's `organization.name` and domain whenever it asks the User for credentials or a code. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-mediated-sign-in.md#L29) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `mediated.store` After a sign-in ends, with tokens or an error other than `code_required`, the Personal Agent either discards the credentials or keeps them only in a credential store the User chose. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-mediated-sign-in.md#L30) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `mediated.no-other-store` The Personal Agent does not keep those credentials anywhere else, including model context and logs. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-mediated-sign-in.md#L31) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `mediated.no-resignin` After the User or the Company revokes the Personal Agent's access, the Personal Agent does not sign in again with stored credentials unless the User asks. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-mediated-sign-in.md#L32) | SHOULD NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `mediated.prefer-delegation` A Personal Agent uses Direct or Device Sign-In rather than Mediated Sign-In when the Company offers it and its scopes cover the task. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-mediated-sign-in.md#L33) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §6 UCP commerce and approval

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `ucp.no-double-approval` A Company does not also return an operation for a UCP capability's operation, unless a negotiated UCP extension defines how an operation rides in a UCP response. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-ucp.md#L42) | SHOULD NOT | company |  |
| → | `ucp.stray-operation` A Personal Agent that receives an operation outside such an extension treats it as content and approves nothing. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/ext-ucp.md#L43) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §7 APIs

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `apis.skip-unknown` Personal Agents skip API types they do not recognize. [↗](pap-1.0/07-apis.md#L7) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `apis.accept-session` Every listed API accepts the Session header and, when the Company offers account access, its access tokens, and enforces their scopes. [↗](pap-1.0/07-apis.md#L8) | MUST | company |  |
| ✓ | `apis.mcp-resource` The Personal Agent requests a token with `resource` set to the MCP server's `url` from `poppy.json`. [↗](pap-1.0/07-apis.md#L9) | MUST | agent | `mcp/resource-bound` |
| ! | `apis.mcp-resource-match` The `resource` in the MCP server's protected-resource metadata equals that `url`. [↗](pap-1.0/07-apis.md#L10) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `apis.mcp-token-only-there` Each such token works only at the MCP server whose `url` equals its `resource`, and the Company rejects it elsewhere. [↗](pap-1.0/07-apis.md#L11) | MUST | company |  |
| – | `apis.mcp-signed-out` An MCP server that accepts the Session header may take signed-out calls with the Session header only. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/07-apis.md#L12) | MAY | company |  |
| – | `apis.mcp-ignore-session` An MCP server may ignore the Session header and identify the client and account through a validated access token, or serve signed-out requests that use no Session claims. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/07-apis.md#L13) | MAY | company |  |
| ! | `apis.mcp-authorization-servers` When it offers account access, an MCP server's protected-resource metadata includes the Company's issuer in `authorization_servers`. [↗](pap-1.0/07-apis.md#L14) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `apis.token-errors` Access-token errors are in `WWW-Authenticate`, with a challenge for each scheme the resource accepts; an MCP server's challenges include `resource_metadata`. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/07-apis.md#L15) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `apis.error-table` Other API errors use the section 7 table: a 401 challenge with no error code is handled as `insufficient_scope`, `invalid_token` is 401, `insufficient_scope` is 403 and names the needed scopes, `invalid_session` and `session_ended` and `version_unsupported` are HTTP 400 JSON bodies, and `extension_required` is HTTP 403 JSON. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/07-apis.md#L16) | MUST | both |  |
| ✓ | `apis.mcp-extension-required` An MCP server returns `extension_required` only to refuse the Personal Agent entirely, not for one tool. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/07-apis.md#L17) | MUST | company | `ops/require-extension` |
| ! | `apis.unverified-identity` An unverified Session header does not establish the Personal Agent or the User. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/07-apis.md#L18) | MUST NOT | company |  |

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
