| – | `ucp.browser-endpoint` A Company may offer `web.browser_session_endpoint`; a `continue_url` does not use it. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-ucp.md#L48) | MAY | company |  |

## §8 UCP sessions and resources

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `ucp.continue-later` The Personal Agent may continue a UCP workflow in a later Session for the same User while the workflow remains available and the Company's access policy allows. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-ucp.md#L52) | MAY | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `ucp.no-reuse-id` The Personal Agent does not reuse one User's UCP workflow identifier for another User. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-ucp.md#L53) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `ucp.no-assume-visible` A Personal Agent does not assume that a cart or checkout it created through UCP appears on the Company's website, in a Company Agent conversation, or in another Session unless the Company says so. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-ucp.md#L54) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| – | `ucp.ignore-or-require` A UCP endpoint may ignore the Session header, and a Company may also require a verified Session header on requests through this extension. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/ext-ucp.md#L55) | MAY | company |  |

## §8.1 Conversation protocols

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `conversations.description` The Company includes a `description` in every `agent.protocols` entry. [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L7) | MUST | company |  |
| – | `conversations.description-any` The description may say the agent can help with anything. [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L8) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `conversations.skip-unknown` The Personal Agent skips unfamiliar conversation protocol types. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L9) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §8.2 Requests

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `conversations.session` Every conversation request carries the Session header, and an access token when signed in. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L13) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `conversations.owner` A request continues a conversation only when the Personal Agent's `client_id`, the User ID that started it, and, once it uses an account, that account all match; any other request is rejected as the ownership table shows. [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L14) | MUST | company |  |
| – | `conversations.version-mismatch` The Company may reject a request on a conversation from a Session that uses a different protocol version or different extension versions, with `version_mismatch` (HTTP 409) and the protocol version the conversation started in as `protocol_version`. [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L15) | MAY | company |  |
| ! | `conversations.id-alphabet` Conversation IDs, request IDs, message IDs and event IDs are strings of 1 to 256 characters from the URL-safe base64 alphabet. [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L16) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `conversations.id-format` The side that did not choose an ID does not depend on its format beyond those rules. [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L17) | MUST NOT | both |  |

## §8.3 Sending messages

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `conversations.create` A new conversation starts with its first message, except when accepting a `user_requested` event without a message, and the Company returns the new conversation's ID. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L21) | MUST | company |  |
| → | `conversations.request-id` Every `POST` body has an `id`, chosen by the Personal Agent, unique for the User across all its requests; a message's ID is its request's ID. [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L22) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `conversations.retry` If the Company has already accepted a request with that ID, path and body, it returns the original response and does not act on the request again; if the path or body is different, it returns `request_id_conflict`. [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L23) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `conversations.order` The Company acts on a conversation's messages, handoff requests and handoff cancels in the order it accepts them, whatever their URL; a close is the exception. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L24) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `conversations.accept-only` A successful `POST` means the Company accepted the request, not that it has acted on it, and the response has only `conversation_id`. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L25) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `conversations.wait` When a `POST` has `wait`, the Company accepts the request and then responds as a read of events from the given cursor, or from the start if there is no cursor, holding the request for up to `wait` seconds, and the status code stays 201 or 202. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L26) | MUST | company |  |

## §8.4 Message fields

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `conversations.ignore-client-fields` The Personal Agent does not send `id` or `role`, and the Company ignores them if sent. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L30) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `conversations.message-content` A message has at least one of `text`, `data`, `context` or `extensions`. [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L31) | MUST | both |  |
| – | `conversations.as-of-request` A Company Agent message with `author.type` `agent` may include `as_of_request`, the ID of the latest Personal Agent request it took into account. [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L32) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `conversations.as-of-cursor` A Personal Agent message with `author.type` `agent` may include `as_of_cursor`, the cursor of the last read it had handled. [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L33) | MAY | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `conversations.as-of-human` A message with `author.type` `human` does not include `as_of_request` or `as_of_cursor`. [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L34) | MUST NOT | both |  |
| ! | `conversations.as-of-optional` The Company and the Personal Agent do not depend on either field being present, and treat each only as a hint. [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L35) | MUST NOT | both |  |
| → | `conversations.context-format` When a Personal Agent shares `locale`, `time_zone` or `user_available`, it uses the field and format defined in section 8.4. [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L36) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `conversations.context-extra` `context` may include other fields, and a Company may ignore them. [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L37) | MAY | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `conversations.context-null` A `context` field set to `null` clears it, and fields a message leaves out keep their previous values. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L38) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `conversations.author-type` `author.type` is `agent` or `human`. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L39) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `conversations.ignore-author-display` A Company ignores `author.id`, `name` and `image` on the Personal Agent's messages. [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L40) | MUST | company |  |
| – | `conversations.author-display` A Company whose messages come from several people or AI personas may set `author.id`, `name` and `image`. [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L41) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `conversations.unknown-role` A Personal Agent treats a message with a `role` it does not recognize as content from the Company. [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L42) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `conversations.unknown-author-type` Either side treats an `author.type` it does not recognize as `agent`. [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L43) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `conversations.extension-version` A side does not send an extension's content unless the other side uses that extension with the same version. [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L44) | MUST NOT | both |  |

## §8.5 Reading events

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `conversations.skip-events` Personal Agents skip event types they do not recognize. [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L48) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `conversations.cursor-opaque` The Personal Agent does not compare or sort cursors. [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L49) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `conversations.wait-cap` `wait` is a whole number of seconds, 0 or more; the Company holds the request until there is an event, until `working` changes from `true` to `false`, or until `wait` seconds, and a larger `wait` than its cap is held only as long as the cap, not rejected. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L50) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `conversations.read-fields` Every successful read includes `conversation_id`, `events`, `cursor`, `has_more`, `working`, `handoff`, `responder` and `closed`, with `events` empty when there are none. [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L51) | MUST | company |  |
| → | `conversations.apply-order` The Personal Agent applies events in order, relies on the state fields once `has_more` is `false`, and skips event IDs it has already handled. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L52) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `conversations.cursor-expired` A cursor for events the Company no longer has returns `cursor_expired`. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L53) | MUST | company |  |

## §8.6 Streaming

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| – | `conversations.stream` A Company may stream events with server-sent events when the read sends `Accept: text/event-stream`, and a Company that does not stream returns JSON. [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L57) | MAY | company |  |
| ! | `conversations.working-event` In a stream, `working` is sent as a `working` event with no SSE `id`, when the stream opens and each time it changes. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L58) | MUST | company |  |
| – | `conversations.stream-close` The Company may close a stream at any time. [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L59) | MAY | company |  |
| ! | `conversations.last-event-id` On reconnect, `Last-Event-ID` is the last event the Personal Agent handled, and if a request has both `Last-Event-ID` and `cursor`, `Last-Event-ID` wins. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L60) | MUST | both |  |
| – | `conversations.text-delta` While the Company Agent writes a message, the Company may send `text-delta` events with no SSE `id`. [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L61) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `conversations.skip-sse` Personal Agents skip stream events with an SSE `event` name they do not recognize. [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L62) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §8.7 State

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `conversations.state-fields` `working`, `handoff`, `responder` and `closed` are independent; a new conversation starts with `handoff` `none`, `responder` `agent` and `closed` `false`. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L66) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `conversations.unknown-state` A Personal Agent treats a `handoff` it does not recognize as `pending`, and a `responder` it does not recognize as `human`. [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L67) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `conversations.state-event` Every change to `handoff`, `responder` or `closed` adds a `state` event with all three, and changes to `working` add no event. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L68) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `conversations.message-author-type` Each Company message includes `author.type`, with `agent` or `human`. [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L69) | MUST | company |  |

## §8.8 Human or AI

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `conversations.author` The Personal Agent sets each message's `author.type` to `agent` when it wrote the message, and to `human` only when the message carries the User's own words; a summary, paraphrase or translation is `agent`. [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L73) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §8.9 Handoff to a person

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `conversations.handoff` A handoff request returns HTTP 202; when the Company acts, `handoff` becomes `pending` until a person joins or nobody is available. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L77) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `conversations.handoff-noop` If `handoff` is already `pending`, or a person is already handling the conversation, the request changes nothing. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L78) | MUST | company |  |
| – | `conversations.handoff-cancel` On a cancel, the Company may stop looking for a person, or may keep looking. [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L79) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `conversations.handoff-cancel-effect` The Personal Agent does not depend on the cancel taking effect. [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L80) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `conversations.handoff-cancel-noop` A cancel when `handoff` is not `pending` changes nothing. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L81) | MUST | company |  |

## §8.10 Direct Conversations

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `conversations.direct-privacy` The Company does not send information in a Direct Conversation that it cannot share with the Personal Agent. [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L85) | MUST NOT | company |  |
| ! | `conversations.direct-parent` The parent conversation is open, belongs to the same owner, and is not itself a Direct Conversation; otherwise the Company returns `conversation_not_found`, `conversation_closed`, `invalid_request` or `direct_conversation_open` as section 8.10 specifies. [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L86) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `conversations.user-requested-state` A `user_requested` event does not change the conversation's state. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L87) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `conversations.user-requested-id` The Company rejects a `user_requested_event_id` that does not name a `user_requested` event in that parent with `invalid_request`. [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L88) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `conversations.direct-omit-message` A request without `message` is valid only when starting a Direct Conversation with both `parent_conversation_id` and `user_requested_event_id`. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L89) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `conversations.direct-retry` Repeating the same parent ID and event ID returns the same Direct Conversation without adding another message, even after it closes. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L90) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `conversations.direct-parent-lock` While a Direct Conversation is open, messages, handoff requests and handoff cancels to the parent return `direct_conversation_open`; closing the parent also closes its open Direct Conversation. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L91) | MUST | company |  |

## §8.11 Sign-in during a conversation

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `conversations.authorization-event` When the Company Agent needs the User's account, it adds an `authorization` event whose `error` is `insufficient_scope` and whose `scope` names the scopes needed. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L95) | MUST | company |  |
| – | `conversations.authorization-header` When a response carrying an `authorization` event has not yet sent its headers, the Company may also include the matching `WWW-Authenticate` challenge. [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L96) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `conversations.authorization-once` The Personal Agent handles the event and a matching challenge as one authorization need, and does not resubmit an accepted message because it received the challenge. [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L97) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `conversations.token-changes` The Personal Agent may start or stop sending an access token partway through a conversation, or continue it in a new Session, as long as the request matches the conversation's owner. [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L98) | MAY | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `conversations.account-challenge` Once a conversation has used the User's account, a request on it for the same User without an access token for that account gets a challenge. [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L99) | MUST | company |  |

## §8.12 Closing

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| – | `conversations.close-drop` A close does not wait its turn; the Company may act on any request it has not acted on yet, or may drop it. [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L103) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `conversations.close-no-depend` The Personal Agent does not depend on either of those outcomes. [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L104) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `conversations.closed` A closed conversation takes no more messages, handoff requests or handoff cancels: they return `conversation_closed`; a close sent to a conversation that is already closed returns HTTP 202 and changes nothing. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L105) | MUST | company |  |

## §8.13 Errors

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `conversations.errors` Conversation errors use the section 8.13 table: `conversation_not_found` 404, `conversation_closed` 409, `direct_conversation_open` 409, `request_id_conflict` 409, `invalid_cursor` 400, `cursor_expired` 410, `invalid_request` 400, `extension_required` 403 and `version_mismatch` 409. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L109) | MUST | both |  |
| → | `conversations.unknown-error` A Personal Agent handles an `error` code it does not recognize by the response's HTTP status. [↗](pap-1.0/08-conversations.md#L110) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §9 Task coverage

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `tasks.no-token` The Personal Agent sends `GET {tasks.endpoint}` with the Session header and no access token. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/09-tasks.md#L7) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| – | `tasks.per-session` A Company may give different Sessions different responses, and verifies the Session header before it does. [↗](pap-1.0/09-tasks.md#L8) | MAY | company |  |
| ! | `tasks.private-cache` A Company that gives different Sessions different responses marks them `private` or `no-store` in `Cache-Control`. [↗](pap-1.0/09-tasks.md#L9) | MUST | company |  |
| → | `tasks.fetch-early` A Personal Agent gets the tasks response before it starts on a task in a Session. [↗](pap-1.0/09-tasks.md#L10) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `tasks.reuse` A Personal Agent may reuse the response for the rest of the Session, as its caching headers allow. [↗](pap-1.0/09-tasks.md#L11) | MAY | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `tasks.other-session` A Personal Agent does not use a tasks response in another Session. [↗](pap-1.0/09-tasks.md#L12) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `tasks.missing` When it gets no response, the Personal Agent carries on as if the Company listed no excluded tasks, published no skills and took no feedback. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/09-tasks.md#L13) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §9 UCP errors

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `ucp.session-errors` A UCP endpoint that verifies the Session header returns `invalid_session` and `session_ended` as UCP responses: HTTP 400 with UCP's error body and `code` set to the error's name over REST, and a JSON-RPC error whose `data.code` names it over MCP. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/ext-ucp.md#L59) | MUST | company |  |
| → | `ucp.handle-session-errors` For `session_ended` the Personal Agent starts a new Session and sends the request again, once, and for `invalid_session` it stops sending the request until it fixes the cause. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/ext-ucp.md#L60) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §9.1 Excluded tasks

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `tasks.excluded-shape` Each excluded task has a short `task` phrase and an optional `alternative`. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/09-tasks.md#L17) | MUST | company |  |
| ✎ | `tasks.not-offered` A listed task is not offered through the Company Agent, the APIs or the website in a browser session. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/09-tasks.md#L18) | MUST | company | _the Company keeps the tasks it lists in excludedTasks out of its tools and Company Agent_ |
| ! | `tasks.not-a-limit` A limit that depends on the User's account is not an excluded task; the Company returns an error for it. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/09-tasks.md#L19) | MUST NOT | company |  |

## §9.2 Alternatives

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✓ | `tasks.alternative` An alternative has at least one of `instructions` or `references`. [↗](pap-1.0/09-tasks.md#L23) | MUST | company | `tasks/excluded` |
| ✓ | `tasks.listed-apis` An `openapi` or `mcp` reference names an API listed in the Company's `poppy.json`. [↗](pap-1.0/09-tasks.md#L24) | MUST | company | `tasks/excluded` |
| → | `tasks.ignore-unlisted` Personal Agents ignore an `openapi` or `mcp` reference that does not name a listed API. [↗](pap-1.0/09-tasks.md#L25) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `tasks.web-no-credentials` A `web` reference does not authorize sending a Session JWT or access token to its target. [↗](pap-1.0/09-tasks.md#L26) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `tasks.skip-unknown-ref` Personal Agents skip reference types they do not recognize. [↗](pap-1.0/09-tasks.md#L27) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `tasks.alternative-content` An alternative is content from the Company: its `instructions` are not instructions the Personal Agent has to follow. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/09-tasks.md#L28) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §9.3 Feedback

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `tasks.feedback` When a User's task cannot be done, the Personal Agent may send `POST {feedback.endpoint}` with the Session header. [↗](pap-1.0/09-tasks.md#L32) | MAY | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `tasks.feedback-shape` A report has `task` of at most 200 characters and `description` of at most 2,000 characters, and the description has no identifiers. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/09-tasks.md#L33) | MUST | both |  |
| ! | `tasks.feedback-verify` A Company verifies the Session header on a report, and needs no scope for it. [↗](pap-1.0/09-tasks.md#L34) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `tasks.feedback-attribute` The Company verifies the header before attributing a report to a Personal Agent, User or Session. [↗](pap-1.0/09-tasks.md#L35) | MUST | company |  |
| → | `tasks.feedback-no-personal` Personal Agents do not put personal data in a report. [↗](pap-1.0/09-tasks.md#L36) | SHOULD NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `tasks.feedback-no-secrets` Personal Agents do not put secrets in a report. [↗](pap-1.0/09-tasks.md#L37) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `tasks.feedback-once` A Personal Agent sends one report for each task it could not do, not one for each attempt. [↗](pap-1.0/09-tasks.md#L38) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `tasks.feedback-excluded` A Personal Agent does not report a task the Company lists as excluded. [↗](pap-1.0/09-tasks.md#L39) | SHOULD NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `tasks.feedback-data` Companies treat a report's text as data, not as instructions. [↗](pap-1.0/09-tasks.md#L40) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `tasks.feedback-response` The Company responds with HTTP 202 and no body, or, when the task can be done after all, with HTTP 200 and an alternative. [↗](pap-1.0/09-tasks.md#L41) | MUST | company |  |
| → | `tasks.feedback-accept` Personal Agents accept either feedback response. [↗](pap-1.0/09-tasks.md#L42) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `tasks.feedback-invalid` A malformed or too-long report gets `invalid_request` (HTTP 400). _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/09-tasks.md#L43) | MUST | company |  |

## §9.4 Agent context

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| – | `tasks.skills` A Company may include `skill_index` in its tasks response. [↗](pap-1.0/09-tasks.md#L47) | MAY | company |  |
| ! | `tasks.skill-format` Companies that publish `skill_index` follow the pinned Agent Skills discovery revision's index format, artifact distribution, integrity and HTTP requirements for artifacts, with the index in the tasks response instead of fetched from its own URL. [↗](pap-1.0/09-tasks.md#L48) | MUST | company |  |
| → | `tasks.skill-verify` Personal Agents that use the index follow its verification and archive safety requirements before using a skill. [↗](pap-1.0/09-tasks.md#L49) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `tasks.skill-ignore` Personal Agents may ignore `skill_index` and use the Company's channels directly. [↗](pap-1.0/09-tasks.md#L50) | MAY | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `tasks.skill-use` Personal Agents may use a skill's descriptions and workflows to carry out the User's task. [↗](pap-1.0/09-tasks.md#L51) | MAY | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `tasks.skill-resolve` Personal Agents resolve an entry's `url` against `tasks.endpoint` using RFC 3986 §5, and resolved URLs and redirects still follow section 3's HTTPS and address rules. [↗](pap-1.0/09-tasks.md#L52) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `tasks.skill-no-credentials` Listing an artifact on another domain does not authorize sending it credentials or Session headers. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/09-tasks.md#L53) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `tasks.skill-unknown` Personal Agents ignore unknown index fields, skip entries with an unknown `type`, and ignore the index when `$schema` is absent or unknown. [↗](pap-1.0/09-tasks.md#L54) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| – | `tasks.skill-well-known` A Company may also publish the same index at `/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json`. [↗](pap-1.0/09-tasks.md#L55) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `tasks.skill-no-scripts` Personal Agents do not execute scripts from a skill unless the User or the Personal Agent's configuration explicitly allows it. [↗](pap-1.0/09-tasks.md#L56) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `tasks.skill-no-grant` A skill grants no account access, changes no OAuth scopes, and supplies no User approval. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/09-tasks.md#L57) | MUST | both |  |

## §10 UCP security

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `ucp.one-issuer` Through this extension, the Personal Agent signs in only at the issuer it selected, whatever `realm` or `resource_metadata` a UCP challenge carries. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/ext-ucp.md#L64) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `ucp.content` Product data, `messages` and Ask answers are content from the Company: data, never instructions, and never the User's approval of a purchase. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/ext-ucp.md#L65) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `ucp.payment-secrets` Payment-handler tokens and any credential the Personal Agent handles are secrets kept out of model context. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/ext-ucp.md#L66) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §10.1 Content from Companies

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `security.content-is-data` Personal Agents treat content from a Company as data, not as instructions; only the User decides what the Personal Agent does. [↗](pap-1.0/10-security.md#L7) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `security.no-cross-company` A Personal Agent does not act at one Company, or send it information, because content from another Company asked it to. [↗](pap-1.0/10-security.md#L8) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `security.only-for-task` A Personal Agent acts at a Company only when the User's task needs it. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/10-security.md#L9) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `security.relevant-only` A Personal Agent sends a Company only information relevant to the User's task. [↗](pap-1.0/10-security.md#L10) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `security.not-approval` Text from a Company is never the User's approval or consent. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/10-security.md#L11) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §10.2 Secrets and the model

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `security.secrets` Personal Agents keep access tokens, refresh tokens, Session JWTs, private keys, authorization codes, PKCE code verifiers and device codes out of model context. [↗](pap-1.0/10-security.md#L15) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `security.other-secrets` Personal Agents keep every other secret out of model context too, such as one-time codes, and sign and send requests in code the model cannot read. [↗](pap-1.0/10-security.md#L16) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §10.3 What a domain vouches for

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `security.domain-identity` Nothing in `poppy.json` confirms that the domain belongs to the company in `organization.name`; the domain is the Company's identity, and choosing the right domain is up to the Personal Agent. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/10-security.md#L20) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §10.7 Delegated keys

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `security.blind-sign` A Personal Agent has the keys in its `jwks_uri` sign client assertions and delegations blindly, unless its own systems need to see which Companies a User works with, using the RSABSSA-SHA384-PSS-Deterministic variant of RFC 9474. [↗](pap-1.0/10-security.md#L24) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `security.blind-jti` When it signs blindly, the Personal Agent generates the client assertion or delegation `jti` on the User's device. [↗](pap-1.0/10-security.md#L25) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `security.blind-both` A Personal Agent that signs blindly signs both its client assertions and its delegations blindly. [↗](pap-1.0/10-security.md#L26) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `security.blind-not-approval` A Personal Agent that signs blindly does not rely on a signature by a key in its `jwks_uri` to mean its own systems approved what it signed. [↗](pap-1.0/10-security.md#L27) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `security.token-on-device` A Personal Agent that signs blindly, or otherwise lets devices get client assertions, keeps refresh and access tokens on the User's device and limits how many signatures each User can get. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/10-security.md#L28) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `security.dpop-per-user` A Personal Agent whose servers hold DPoP keys signs with a User's key only for that User. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/10-security.md#L29) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## §10.8 Sign-ins someone else started

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `security.list-scopes` In Direct and Device Sign-In, the Company's consent page lists every scope it will grant, except a `poppy:browser-sign-in` it may grant without asking, and it may mark the ones the User already granted. [↗](pap-1.0/10-security.md#L33) | MUST | company |  |
| → | `security.prompt-unless-same-device` A Personal Agent sends `prompt=consent` unless the redirect comes back to the device that opened the authorization URL. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/10-security.md#L34) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## Operations 2 Advertising support

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `ops.website-endpoint` A Company that asks for approval on its website lists an HTTPS `endpoint` and `web.browser_session_endpoint`; a Company that returns no operations on its website does not list or serve `endpoint`. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L7) | MUST | company |  |
| ✓ | `ops.require-extension` A Company does not return operations in response to a request that does not declare operations version 3; it handles approval itself or refuses with `extension_required` and `extension` set to `operations`. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L8) | MUST NOT | company | `ops/require-extension` |
| ✓ | `ops.mcp-tool-error` An MCP tool that needs the extension returns an ordinary tool error to a Personal Agent that does not declare it, since an MCP server returns `extension_required` only to refuse the Personal Agent entirely. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L9) | MUST | company | `ops/require-extension` |

## Operations 3 The operation

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `ops.id-reuse` The Company does not use an `operation_id` for another action. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L13) | MUST NOT | company |  |
| ! | `ops.revision-changes` The Company changes `revision` whenever the terms or `expires_at` change. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L14) | MUST | company |  |
| ✎ | `ops.complete-terms` Everything that affects the action is in the revision's `terms`, and in `summary` if present. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L15) | MUST | company | _the summary and terms are written by the Company's own handlers_ |
| ✓ | `ops.perform-confirmed-only` The Company performs only what the approved revision describes. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L16) | MUST | company | `ops/performs` |
| ✓ | `ops.no-early-start` The Company does not start the action before it receives an approval for it. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L17) | MUST NOT | company | `ops/performs` |
| – | `ops.summary-markdown` A `summary` may use emphasis, strong emphasis, paragraphs and lists. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L18) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `ops.summary-render` A Personal Agent may render those elements or show the text as is. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L19) | MAY | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `ops.summary-no-links` The Personal Agent does not render links, images or HTML in a `summary`, and shows them as text. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L20) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `ops.unique-revision` The Company does not give two different sets of terms the same `revision`. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L21) | MUST NOT | company |  |
| ✓ | `ops.at-most-once` Whichever revision is approved, the Company performs each operation at most once. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L22) | MUST | company | `ops/confirm`<br>`ops/performs`<br>`ops/website-confirm` |
| ! | `ops.expires-long-enough` `expires_at` leaves the User long enough to read the terms and decide, unless the Company cannot hold the terms that long. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L23) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `ops.who-approves` An operation returned signed out can be approved only while signed out; one returned signed in belongs to the account and can be approved only while signed in to the same account, in any Session of the same Personal Agent and User; a signed-out Session of that Personal Agent and User gets a challenge. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L24) | MUST | company |  |

## Operations 4 Asking for approval

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `ops.api-shape` An API that wants approval responds with HTTP 403 and a JSON body with `error` `approval_required` and the operation in `operation`, not in `WWW-Authenticate`. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L28) | MUST | company |  |
| – | `ops.api-extra` That body may have other members. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L29) | MAY | company |  |
| ! | `ops.mcp-shape` An MCP tool returns an error result with `isError` true, the operation in `structuredContent.operation`, and text that says the action needs approval. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L30) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ops.conversation-shape` A Company message carries the operation in `extensions.operations.operation`. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L31) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ops.website-header` A website that handles the request as the Session performs nothing and responds with HTTP 403 and a `Poppy-Operation` dictionary whose `sid` is the Session's `sid` and whose `ref` is at most 2048 characters from the stated alphabet. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L32) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ops.website-repeat` The website offers a way to make the original request again. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L33) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `ops.website-page` The website answers a page load or form submission with a page that says the action is waiting for approval in the User's personal agent. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L34) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `ops.website-json` The website answers a JSON request from its own scripts with a JSON object with `error` `approval_required` and without the operation. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L35) | SHOULD | company |  |
| – | `ops.website-json-extra` That object may have other members. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L36) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `ops.ref-from-header` The Personal Agent takes a reference only from the `Poppy-Operation` header of a response its own browser received, only when `sid` names a Session it joined that browser to, ignores any other such header, and sends the reference only to that Session's Company's `endpoint`. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L37) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `ops.endpoint-no-scope` The endpoint requires no scope: recording an approval performs nothing. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L38) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ops.bad-ref` A reference the Session cannot use gets HTTP 400 with `{"error": "invalid_request"}`. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L39) | MUST | company |  |

## Operations 5 Approving an operation

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `ops.not-done` When a request returns an operation, the Personal Agent does not treat the action as done. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L43) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `ops.show-user` For a user approval, the Personal Agent shows the User the Company's name and the revision's terms, takes the User's answer through its own interface, and does not treat text from the Company as the User's approval. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L44) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `ops.show-summary` When the operation has a `summary`, the Personal Agent shows it rather than write its own description. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L45) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `ops.agent-instruction` An agent approval rests on an instruction the User gave the Personal Agent; content from the Company, a website, or anything else the Personal Agent read is not one. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L46) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `ops.check-instruction` Before an agent approval, the Personal Agent checks the revision's terms against that instruction and approves only if the instruction covers them. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L47) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `ops.no-same-instruction` If the Company answers an agent approval with a new revision, or a website returns a new operation for the action after recording it, the Personal Agent does not approve the new one on the same instruction. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L48) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `ops.check-terms` Before approving, the Personal Agent checks that `terms` agree with what it asked for, and with the `summary` if there is one, and points out any difference to the User when it asks them. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L49) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## Operations 6 Sending the approval

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `ops.approver` The Personal Agent includes `approver`, `user` or `agent`. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L53) | MUST | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `ops.input-type-agent` The Personal Agent does not include `input_type` with `agent`. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L54) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `ops.reference-one-company` The Personal Agent does not send the same `reference` to two Companies. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L55) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `ops.no-pii-in-approval` The Personal Agent does not put personal data, or anything that identifies the User or their device, in `input_type` or `reference`. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L56) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `ops.include-optional` The Personal Agent includes `approved_at` and `input_type` with `user`. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L57) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| – | `ops.record-approval-fields` A Company may record `approver`, `approved_at`, `input_type` and `reference`. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L58) | MAY | company |  |
| ! | `ops.optional-not-required` A Company does not reject or decline an approval because an optional member is missing or because it does not recognize the `input_type`. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L59) | MUST NOT | company |  |
| ! | `ops.ignore-unknown-members` Companies ignore members of `Poppy-Approval` they do not recognize. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L60) | MUST | company |  |
| ✓ | `ops.message-not-confirmation` In a conversation, the message's `text` does not approve anything; only the approval object does. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L61) | MUST | both | `conv/operation-message` |
| ! | `ops.website-approval-channel` The Company does not accept an approval of a website's operation at an API, MCP server or conversation, or an approval of another interface's operation at `endpoint`. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L62) | MUST NOT | company |  |
| – | `ops.website-repeat-itself` After recording an approval, the website may make the original request again itself. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L63) | MAY | company |  |
| ! | `ops.keep-recorded` The Company keeps a recorded approval that is not used up until the approved revision's `expires_at`, and does not apply it to requests from a Session that cannot approve the operation. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L64) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ops.checks` Before performing the action, the Company checks that the Session can approve the operation, that it has not already been performed, and that the `revision` is one it returned, has not expired, and the request asks for exactly what it describes, and responds as the first failing check says. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L65) | MUST | company |  |
| – | `ops.inconsequential` The Company may ignore differences it considers inconsequential, and may treat a revision it has replaced as failing the revision check. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L66) | MAY | company |  |
| ! | `ops.no-same-revision` A Company does not answer an approval with the revision it names. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L67) | MUST NOT | company |  |
| – | `ops.decline` Once the checks pass, a Company may decline the approval instead of performing the action, performs nothing, and returns no new operation. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L68) | MAY | company |  |
| ! | `ops.decline-reason` The Company does not put anything in `reason` that the Session could not already see. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L69) | MUST NOT | company |  |
| ! | `ops.no-record-declined` The Company does not record a declined approval. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L70) | MUST NOT | company |  |
| → | `ops.no-resend-declined` When an approval is declined, the Personal Agent does not send that approval again, and does not approve a new revision for the same action without asking the User. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L71) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## Operations 7 Retries and at most once

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `ops.remember-performed` The Company remembers that it performed an operation at least until the approved revision's `expires_at`, and while it is being performed. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L75) | MUST | company |  |
| – | `ops.forget-after` After that, the Company may forget it. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L76) | MAY | company |  |
| ! | `ops.retry-same-response` A request with the approval of an operation already performed gets the response the Company gave the first time, or one that says the same, for as long as the Company remembers the operation. _(implied)_ [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L77) | MUST | company |  |
| ! | `ops.unknown-not-failed` While an operation is being performed, or the Company does not know whether it took effect, the Company does not respond as if it failed. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L78) | MUST NOT | company |  |
| → | `ops.no-new-until-known` If a request with an approval fails or times out, the Personal Agent sends it again with the same approval, and does not approve a new operation for the same action, or ask the User to, until it knows whether the first one was performed. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L79) | MUST NOT | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## Operations 8 Security considerations

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| – | `ops.revoke-false-approval` A Company may revoke the `client_id` of a Personal Agent that sends an approval the User did not give or instruct. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L83) | MAY | company |  |
| → | `ops.website-check-action` On a website, the Personal Agent checks that the operation is for the action its browser just took, and points out any difference to the User. [↗](pap-1.0/ext-operations.md#L84) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## Guides: For both parties

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ✎ | `guide.secrets` Keep access tokens, refresh tokens, private keys, client assertions, Session JWTs, DPoP proofs, authorization codes, PKCE code verifiers, device codes, one-time codes, browser-session codes and mediated credentials out of logs, telemetry, error reports, model context, conversation messages and URLs, and redact the `Authorization`, `Poppy-Session`, `DPoP` and `Cookie` headers and credential fields before logging. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L9) | SHOULD | both | _Poppyseed never logs tokens or request bodies; review with each change to logging_ |
| ✓ | `guide.no-store` Send `Cache-Control: no-store` on every response that carries a token or code. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L10) | SHOULD | company | `sessions/token-response-not-cached` |
| ✓ | `guide.algorithms` Sign Session JWTs with ES256; sign client assertions and delegations with ES256 or, when signing blindly, PS384; accept both; use RSA keys of 2048 to 4096 bits; reject `alg: none` and symmetric algorithms. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L11) | SHOULD | both | `guide/jwt-algorithms` |
| ✓ | `guide.assertion-keys` Verify client assertions and delegations only with keys from the verified `jwks_uri`, and Session JWTs only with the key their verified delegation names, ignoring `jku`, `x5u` and any other embedded key. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L12) | SHOULD | company | `identity/assertion-lifetime` |
| ✓ | `guide.assertion-time` Check `aud` and `iat`, and `exp` on client assertions and delegations; accept Session JWTs only within the `iat` window; allow about 30 seconds of clock skew; reject assertions that claim a long lifetime. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L13) | SHOULD | company | `identity/assertion-lifetime`<br>`identity/assertion-fresh` |
| ✓ | `guide.jti-entropy` Make each `jti`, and each Session ID, at least 128 random bits. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L14) | SHOULD | both | `guide/jti-entropy`<br>`dpop/jti-entropy` |
| → | `guide.assertion-exp` Set a client assertion's `exp` at most five minutes after its `iat`. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L15) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ! | `guide.replay-jti` Reject a reused client-assertion `jti` from the same `client_id` until it expires. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L16) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.operator-signature` Build the body, any DPoP proof and the Session JWT before the operator signature; keep operator keys separate from delegated Session keys; do not send devices a shared operator private key; verify the Session JWT's exact `iss` before accepting the client; test the edge and origin together and protect the origin from forged forwarding headers. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L17) | SHOULD | both |  |
| ! | `guide.key-rotation` Give every `jwks_uri` key a `kid`, publish a new key before signing with it, keep an old public key published until everything signed with it has expired, and do not rotate the DPoP key a refresh token was issued with. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L18) | SHOULD | both |  |
| ✓ | `guide.refetch-on-unknown-kid` Refetch `jwks_uri` when an unknown `kid` appears, at most once per interval such as 30 seconds, counting failed fetches too. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L19) | SHOULD | company | `identity/metadata-fetch-bounded` |
| ✎ | `guide.fetch-limits` Limit metadata fetches to a few redirects, a response size such as 100 KB and a timeout of a few seconds, and validate HTTPS certificates. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L20) | SHOULD | both | _redirects are not followed, bodies over 100 KB are cut off, fetches time out after 5 s; covered by core review_ |
| ✓ | `guide.metadata-no-credentials` Never send cookies, tokens or other credentials on metadata fetches. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L21) | SHOULD | both | `guide/metadata-fetch-credentials` |
| ✓ | `guide.private-addresses` Reject loopback, private and link-local addresses unless configured on purpose, checking the address actually connected to. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L22) | SHOULD | both | `identity/private-agent-urls`<br>_on Node the metadata fetch checks the address it connects to (packages/core/src/safe-fetch.ts); core unit test packages/core/test/safe-fetch.test.ts_ |
| ✎ | `guide.cache-bounds` Cache metadata according to HTTP caching headers, within bounds such as at least a minute and at most a day. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L23) | SHOULD | both | _client metadata is cached for its max-age, between a minute and a day; core unit test packages/core/test/client-cache.test.ts_ |
| ! | `guide.explicit-replies` Make an answer or approval explicit about the question or action it addresses, and treat a short reply that could answer more than one open question as answering none of them. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L24) | SHOULD | both |  |
| ✓ | `guide.idempotency-key` Send an `Idempotency-Key` (a random UUID v4) on API writes that accept one, and as a Company keep idempotency records per `client_id`, User ID and account for a set time, returning the original response for a repeated key and rejecting a repeated key with a different body. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L25) | SHOULD | both | `guide/idempotency-key` |
| ✓ | `guide.retries` Each retry needs a new Session JWT, a new DPoP proof when the token is DPoP-bound, and a new assertion for a token request; wait at least `Retry-After` on 429 or 503, and otherwise back off exponentially with jitter. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L26) | SHOULD | both | `ops/in-progress` |
| ✓ | `guide.rate-limits` Limit by `client_id`, by User and by Session, counting a request against a `client_id` only after its Session JWT or client assertion's signature checks pass, and send the `RateLimit` and `RateLimit-Policy` headers. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L27) | SHOULD | company | `tokens/rate-limit` |
| → | `guide.agent-rate-limits` Track each Company's limits across tasks and Users, prefer long polling or streaming over short polls, and spread work that is not time-sensitive outside busy hours. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L28) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| ✓ | `guide.json` Use TLS 1.2 or later, encode JSON as UTF-8, reject objects with duplicate member names, write timestamps in RFC 3339 with an offset, and ignore unrecognized fields. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L29) | SHOULD | both | `guide/json` |
| ! | `guide.mcp-ucp` Follow the MCP lifecycle of the negotiated version, keep Poppy `sid` distinct from `Mcp-Session-Id`, cache MCP results per User and Session when those affect the result, and do not assume one token or signature works for both Poppy and UCP. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L30) | SHOULD | both |  |

## Guides: For personal agents

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| → | `guide.discovery` When the Company reached is on a different domain from the one the User asked for, tell the User the `organization.name` and domain before signing in or acting, and show that the name is unconfirmed; show `logo_uri` next to the domain, never in place of it. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L34) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.versions` Change protocol and extension versions only at a new Session, declare only extensions the Company lists, and record the versions each conversation started in so a `version_mismatch` can be finished in a Session that still uses them. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L35) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.user-ids` Make User IDs random per User and Company, or derive them with a keyed hash of a random internal ID and the Company's identifier, key them by the full issuer or the issuerless HTTPS domain, and tell Users that Companies recognize them across signed-out visits. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L36) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.anonymous` For anonymous browsing, create a random User ID for each browsing session, give it its own `sid` and delegated keys, discard it when the session ends, and never send an access token with it. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L37) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.session-header` Decide Session-header destinations from `poppy.json` and listed API descriptions, keep the header off discovery and OAuth requests, sign a new JWT per request where the final method and URL are known, round delegation `iat` down, and on `invalid_session` fix the JWT instead of starting a new Session. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L38) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.token-storage` Encrypt refresh tokens at rest away from the model, keep access tokens in memory, key them by the Company's full issuer, request a resource-specific token when protected-resource metadata requires one, and on `invalid_grant` continue signed out. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L39) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.plan-access` Read OpenAPI security requirements and MCP authorization discovery before calling, use a refresh token that covers the task before asking the User to sign in, and do not automatically reconnect an account the User disconnected. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L40) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.sign-in-choice` Prefer Direct or Device Sign-In to Mediated Sign-In, and Direct to Device; use descriptions and `auth.scope_hints`, treating a scope without hints as `irreversible` with personal data; ask for the fewest scopes the task needs; and do not send the User to sign in again for a scope the response omitted. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L41) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.direct-device` Open the authorization URL in the User's own browser, make `state` random and single-use, use PKCE with `S256`, use PAR when the endpoint is listed, and for Device Sign-In show `verification_uri_complete` with `user_code` and poll no faster than `interval`. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L42) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.agent-mediated` Collect mediated fields in a form the model never sees, look up stored credentials by the issuer, and do not sign in again with stored credentials after the User disconnects the Personal Agent. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L43) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.distributed-apps` Keep the signing private key on a server, keep delegated keys and DPoP keys in the device's platform keystore with the refresh token they belong to, and return to a phone app through an HTTPS link it claims or Device Sign-In. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L44) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.browsing` Do not browse a Company that sets `web.disabled`; use a separate browser storage context per Session; never type the User's credentials into a website; read the browser-session code only from the endpoint's page; and close the context when the Session ends. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L45) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.agent-conversations` Read until `working` is `false`, use `as_of_request` and `as_of_cursor`, show disclosures and link domains, withdraw a handoff that is no longer needed, and close a Direct Conversation before continuing in the parent. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L46) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.interfaces` Prefer a Company's APIs and Company Agent over browsing, do not phone a Company that publishes a `poppy.json`, and skip API types and conversation protocols you do not recognize. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L47) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.excluded-tasks` Get the tasks response early in each Session, tell the User when a task is excluded, offer the alternative, and try an alternative from feedback before saying the task cannot be done. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L48) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |
| → | `guide.agent-operations` Show the Company's `summary` or every value in `terms`, check `terms` against what was asked, approve only on the User's instruction, send the saved request with the approval, and on a website take `Poppy-Operation` only from the browser's responses. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L49) | SHOULD | agent | _agent conformance_ |

## Guides: For companies

| | Requirement | Level | Role | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ! | `guide.adoption` Publish `poppy.json` with at least one channel, then add signed-out APIs, Session verification, OAuth, browser join, excluded tasks, feedback and extensions independently as the tasks need them. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L53) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.serve-versions` Publish each protocol version as its own document on the same host, tell endpoints apart by `Poppy-Version`, and retire a version with `Deprecation` and `Sunset` before removing it. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L54) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.signed-out-no-oauth` Offer signed-out Sessions without an authorization server by returning 404 or empty `authorization_servers`, and set `auth.disabled` rather than dropping an issuer you are not ready to open. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L55) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.company-agents` Fetch `client_id` without following redirects, cache client metadata, keep allowlists or blocklists, and publish `client_id_metadata_document_supported` when the authorization server accepts client ID metadata documents. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L56) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.verify-session` Verify the Session header in one place, cache a verified delegation by a hash of the whole delegation, compare `htu` with the configured public origin, use about a one-minute `iat` window, and do not use unverified claims for attribution or state. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L57) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.sessions` Share Session state across servers, record the User ID and Agent ID a Session starts with, remember ended `sid`s, and use separate Sessions for separate accounts. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L58) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.lifetimes` Give access tokens a lifetime of hours, invalidate them at sign-out or keep them to a few minutes, do not stop accepted work because an access token expired, and bind refresh tokens to their DPoP key where account access has meaningful consequences. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L59) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ✎ | `guide.scope-descriptions` Describe each scope so it says what it unlocks, which tasks need it, and whether the task can be done without it, and give `auth.scope_hints` only when you are sure. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L60) | SHOULD | company | _written by each Company in `scopes`_ |
| ! | `guide.api-descriptions` If you offer Direct or Device Sign-In, make scopes and APIs cover the tasks Users ask for, and write API and MCP descriptions for the model that reads them. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L61) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ✓ | `guide.consent-page` Name the Personal Agent as wanting to connect, show its `client_id` domain, list every scope including ones already granted, show the page for `prompt=consent` and for every Device Sign-In, accept PKCE `S256` only, and return `iss` on every redirect. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L62) | SHOULD | company | `direct/consent-page` |
| ✓ | `guide.device` Offer Direct Sign-In as well, follow RFC 10027 §2, put the verification page on the issuer's host or the Company's domain, and keep `expires_in` short. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L63) | SHOULD | company | `device/abuse` |
| ✓ | `guide.company-mediated` Offer Mediated Sign-In only until Direct or Device Sign-In can replace it; rate-limit attempts, require a one-time code when a sign-in looks unusual, and never store raw credentials. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L64) | SHOULD | company | `mediated/failures` |
| ✓ | `guide.account-settings` List each connected Personal Agent and offer a control that disconnects it by revoking its refresh tokens. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L65) | SHOULD | company | `signout/disconnect` |
| ! | `guide.company-browsing` Choose one of the four website levels, and if you offer OAuth and allow browsing, list `browser_session_endpoint`; make join codes at least 128 bits, use the `__Host-poppy_join` cookie, and send the page with `no-store`, `frame-ancestors 'none'` and `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin`. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L66) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ✓ | `guide.scopes-everywhere` Apply the same scope checks on the website, APIs, Company Agent and live agents, and show a visible error that names missing scopes. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L67) | SHOULD | company | `signin/partial-approval` |
| ! | `guide.internal` Verify access tokens and Session JWTs at the edge, and do not forward them from one internal service to another. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L68) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ✎ | `guide.hosting` Give each hosted Company its own issuer, publish that issuer's metadata and each storefront's `poppy.json` on the storefront's domain, and check the issuer on every request. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L69) | SHOULD | company | _a provider runs one definePoppyseed per hosted Company, each with its own baseUrl as issuer and its own store_ |
| ! | `guide.conversation-provider` Point `agent.protocols` at the provider's endpoint, publish that URL as its own protected resource, and keep the Session JWT audience as the Company's identifier. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L70) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.less-access` Limit scopes by client, refuse a sign-in type with `unauthorized_client`, or set `auth.disabled`, and choose the issuer before launch. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L71) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.guest` Let a signed-out Session do what a signed-out visitor can do, and limit abuse with rate limits by `client_id`. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L72) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ✓ | `guide.company-conversations` Report `working` from acceptance until the reply is finished, set `as_of_request` on Company Agent messages, keep events at least 30 days, and ask for sign-in with an `authorization` event rather than verification questions in messages. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L73) | SHOULD | company | `conv/account-bound` |
| ✓ | `guide.company-excluded-tasks` List tasks you chose not to offer, give an alternative when there is one, and when feedback asks for a task you do offer, answer with an alternative. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L74) | SHOULD | company | `tasks/excluded` |
| ! | `guide.company-operations` Put everything that affects the action in `terms`, send a `summary` when you want your wording shown, derive downstream idempotency keys from the operation ID, and pass a 403 with `Poppy-Operation` through unchanged. [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L75) | SHOULD | company |  |
| ! | `guide.errors` Keep `error_description` free of account details, and return the same error for "does not exist" and "belongs to someone else". [↗](pap-1.0/guides.md#L76) | SHOULD | company |  |
